articles.title: Happiness appears to lead to a sense of purpose, but not the other way around, according to new psychology research
articles.summary: People often assume that finding a mission in life leads to greater happiness, but new research suggests the opposite sequence might be more accurate. Feeling good may provide the emotional foundation necessary to pursue long-term life goals.

articles.title: People with depression who use psilocybin are not abandoning standard mental health care, study suggests
articles.summary: People with depression who use psilocybin mushrooms access standard psychiatric care at roughly the same rates as nonusers, a national U.S. survey finds, yet more than half still report an unmet need for mental health treatment.

articles.title: Psychology says frequent worry isn’t a sure sign of shorter nights — it tracks with reporting less sleep, but not what wrist monitors recorded
articles.summary: People who lean toward worry often feel convinced they aren't getting enough sleep. New psychology research in young adults finds that while higher neuroticism tracks with reporting fewer hours, wrist-worn sleep monitors show no shortfall.

articles.title: Scientists used a Harry Potter soundtrack and implanted electrodes to challenge a common assumption about how we hear
articles.summary: Using electrodes implanted inside the brain and a Harry Potter soundtrack, scientists tested how we separate dialogue from music. Their findings in Science Advances suggest the brain may not need special detectors to tell the two apart.

articles.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces, sensor readings, or environment changes may be unavailable, distorted, or poorly selected. articles.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. Existing evaluations often provide isolated theorem statements in settings where much of this supporting theory is already available in Mathlib. We introduce AutoformBench, a benchmark of 341 Lean 4 formalization tasks drawn from 24 advanced mathematical sources

articles.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Signature Forgery Detection
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Offline handwritten signatures remain a primary behavioural biometric in legal and financial documents. articles.title: The surprising reason women seem better at multitasking than men
articles.summary: Men and women appear to be similarly capable of multitasking, but men are more than twice as likely to ignore conversation while juggling multiple activities. Researchers believe this unexpected difference may help explain why women are widely perceived as better multitaskers.

articles.title: Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety
articles.summary: An AI-powered analysis of thousands of children's brain scans has revealed three distinct brain types underlying ADHD and anxiety that do not neatly fit traditional diagnoses. These hidden biological patterns can appear before a diagnosis is made, potentially enabling earlier detection and more effective, personalized treatments.
